definition: AI washing is a deceptive marketing tactic that consists of promoting a product or a service by overstating the role of artificial intelligence (AI) and the integration of it.
details: Companies often involve in the practice to mislead customers to boost their offerings, and to secure funding from investors. The practice raises concerns regarding transparency, and legal issues.

explainer.lead: A label such as “AI-powered” can make an offering sound more capable than it really is. AI washing matters because exaggerated claims can distort buying and investment decisions, weaken trust, and create legal exposure.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a cereal box saying a robot invented the recipe when people actually did the work. That is like AI washing: a company makes AI sound important to get attention or money. It is fairer to explain what the AI really did and let people judge the product itself.
tiers.practitioner: When assessing an AI claim, ask what the AI actually does, where it contributes to design or operation, and what evidence supports the claim beyond labels such as “smart” or “AI-powered.” Evaluate the delivered product or service as a whole rather than treating AI involvement as proof of value. For layoff claims, separate demonstrated AI productivity effects from other possible motives such as cost-cutting.
tiers.paperLevel: AI washing = deceptive promotion of a product or service through overstatement of AI’s role or integration, including claiming AI involvement when none occurred or misusing AI terminology. The term was defined by the AI Now Institute at New York University in 2019 and derives from greenwashing. It defines no quantitative threshold for sufficient AI involvement; a 2026 usage also covers attributing layoffs to AI capabilities when the cuts may be unrelated.

explainer.example: In September 2023, Coca-Cola released Coca-Cola Y3000 and said the flavor had been “co-created with human and artificial intelligence.” The company was accused of AI washing because it provided no proof of AI involvement, leading critics to argue that AI served mainly to attract consumer attention.

usedIn.name: Coca-Cola Y3000
usedIn.detail: Released in September 2023 and described as co-created with humans and AI; critics accused the company of AI washing because AI involvement was not demonstrated.

usedIn.name: Investment fundraising
usedIn.detail: Companies may exaggerate AI use to attract funding, and misleading AI statements have drawn enforcement from the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

usedIn.name: Layoff explanations
usedIn.detail: In 2026, some technology companies were accused of blaming workforce reductions on AI productivity when cost-cutting and profitability may have been the motives.

explainer.intuition: AI washing substitutes an attractive AI story for a clear account of what the technology actually contributes. Like greenwashing, it exploits interest in a popular idea to make an offering appear more impressive.
howItWorks: A company seeks attention, sales, competitive advantage, or investment.
It promotes its offering with claims such as “AI-powered” or “co-created with AI.”
The AI role is absent, overstated, unclear, or described with misused terminology.
Customers or investors may act on the inflated impression, creating deception, transparency, trust, and legal concerns.
explainer.whyItMatters: AI washing can mislead customers and investors, reduce transparency, and damage trust in legitimate AI work. In March 2024, the US Securities and Exchange Commission imposed its first civil penalties on two companies for misleading statements about AI use; in July 2024, it charged an executive at a supposed AI hiring startup with fraud over AI-related buzzwords.
misconceptions: Not every AI marketing claim is AI washing; the problem is deception, overstatement, or misuse of the term.
Calling a product “smart” or “AI-powered” does not by itself establish a meaningful AI contribution.
AI washing is not limited to product features; the term has also been applied to questionable claims that AI caused layoffs.
